newsitem.title: USA: WHX reports big loss, cites steelworkers' strike.
newsitem.headline: WHX reports big loss, cites steelworkers' strike.

text.p: Steelmaker WHX Corp. Friday reported a loss for the second quarter due to the effects of a 10-month-long strike that was settled last week.
WHX said it lost $31.1 million, or $1.58 a share, in the quarter ended June 30, compared with profits of $16.8 million, or 42 cents a share, a year earlier.
Sales tumbled 64 percent to $128.5 million from $357.8 million.
The results beat expectations on Wall Street but WHX stock fell 12.5 cents to $10.125 in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Some 4,500 members of the United Steelworkers of America union went on strike against WHX unit Wheeling-Pittsburgh Corp. in October, idling eight steel plants in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.
By the time a tentative contract agreement was reached last week, the strike had become the longest major walkout ever at a U.S. steelmaker.
Wheeling-Pittsburgh, based in Wheeling, W. Va., was forced to halt all raw steel production during the strike. It produced about 598,000 tons of raw steel in the second quarter of 1996.
Shipments of steel products totaled 165,714 tons in the most recent quarter, down from 673,408 tons a year ago.
The company expects to resume production at the idled plants later this month, a spokesman said.
